To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Grp1 family of Arf GEFs are potently autoinhibted by a pseudosubstate mechanism, and that the autoinhibtion is relieved by binding of active GTP-Arf to the GEF and by phosphorylation.
the Grp1 family of Arf GEFs is autoinhibited by a mechanism involving the Sec7 and PH domains, which is relieved by binding of active GTP-bound Arf6 or by phosphorylation of the PH domain by PKC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which Arf GEFs are recruited to membranes and how this recruitment is coupled to activation of the Sec7 catalytic domain.
the mechanisms of autoregulatory mechanisms of Arf GEFs and their role in membrane trafficking.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate Arf GEFs, which play a critical role in the control of vesicle trafficking and cell polarity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Grp1 family of Arf GEFs are autoinhibited by a pseudosubstate mechanism that is relieved by binding of Arf6 to the Sec7 domain and/or phosphorylation of tandem sites within the PH domain.
